title: Dermatology & MedSpa Office Rates: Per-Sq-Ft and Monthly Cleaning Cost Benchmarks
seoTitle: Dermatology & MedSpa Office Rates: Cleaning Cost per Sq Ft & Month
metaDescription: Dermatology medspa office rates run $0.09–$0.20/sq ft per visit, or about $3,200–$11,700/month for 1,800–3,200 sq ft. Compare bids with our calculator.
excerpt: Dermatology and medspa suites price above general office space because treatment rooms, hard flooring, and patient restrooms add labor to every visit. This guide breaks down per-sq-ft rates, monthly totals by suite size, and the frequency most practices actually need.
quickAnswer: Most dermatology and medspa suites pay $0.12–$0.20 per sq ft per visit under 2,500 sq ft and $0.09–$0.15 per sq ft per visit from 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, before restroom and add-on charges. A typical 3,200 sq ft suite with LVT flooring and three restrooms lands around $4,300–$7,300 per month at three visits a week and $6,800–$11,700 per month at five nightly visits. Treatment-room turnover, hard-surface disinfection, and patient restroom density are what push these suites above a standard office.

blocks.text: Why Dermatology and MedSpa Suites Cost More Than a Standard Office

A dermatology practice or medspa looks like an office on a floor plan, but janitorial crews price it closer to light clinical space. The reason is simple: the share of square footage that needs disinfection rather than a dust-and-vacuum pass is much higher. Exam rooms, procedure rooms for excisions and biopsies, injectables bays, laser rooms, and facial treatment rooms all have padded tables, counters, sinks, and rolling stools that are touched by patients with open skin, numbing creams, peels, and post-procedure product. A typical general office might have 10 to 15 percent of its area in restrooms and kitchens; a 3,200 sq ft medspa often has 45 to 55 percent of its footprint in rooms that require an EPA-registered disinfectant with a verified dwell time.

Hard flooring compounds the effect. Most suites use LVT or sealed porcelain tile in treatment areas because carpet cannot be disinfected and holds hair, product, and shed skin. Hard floors cost more to maintain per visit than carpet because they need daily damp mopping in addition to dust mopping, and grout lines in tiled restrooms add scrubbing time. On top of that, the front of house is a retail-grade showroom: glass shelving for skincare product, a reception desk patients lean on, and a waiting area that has to look spotless when the first injectables patient walks in at 8 a.m.
Per-Sq-Ft Rate Benchmarks by Suite Size

The national per-visit rate bands below are the same benchmarks our Office Cleaning Cost Calculator uses. They apply to the base cleanable area before restrooms, flooring multipliers, and frequency adjustments. Dermatology and medspa operators should expect to land in the middle-to-upper part of each band, because treatment-room disinfection and LVT damp mopping slow production rates below the 3,500 sq ft per hour ISSA benchmark that general offices achieve.

blocks.title: The 2,500 sq ft bracket cliff
blocks.text: Because suites under 2,500 sq ft fall into a higher per-sq-ft band, a 2,400 sq ft medspa can pay nearly the same per visit as a 3,000 sq ft one. If you are near the line, confirm the vendor measured cleanable area the same way your lease does, and ask whether storage rooms, mechanical closets, and the laser equipment room are included or excluded.
Monthly Cost Scenarios for Real Suite Layouts

Per-visit rates only become useful once you multiply them by visits. Our model uses 4.33 weeks per month, so three visits a week equals 13 visits and five nightly visits equals 21.65 visits. Frequency also changes the per-visit price: crews discount daily service by about 10 percent because each visit carries less accumulated soil, while three-times-weekly service gets about a 5 percent discount versus a twice-weekly baseline. The scenarios below assume LVT treatment-room flooring at a 1.04 multiplier and include restroom charges.

blocks.text: Two patterns stand out. First, going from three to five visits a week raises the monthly bill by roughly 60 percent even though per-visit pricing falls slightly. Second, switching treatment-room floors from LVT to tile adds about 6 to 7 percent, largely from grout scrubbing. If you are building out a new suite, that flooring choice has a 10-year janitorial cost attached to it.

Dermatology practices see high patient throughput: a busy general dermatologist can see 30 to 40 patients a day, and a medspa running two injectors and a laser tech can turn 25 to 35 appointments. Many patients change clothes for full-body skin checks or body contouring, so restrooms double as changing areas. Plan on one restroom per 1,000 to 1,200 sq ft, compared with one per 2,500 sq ft in a typical professional office. Each restroom adds $15 to $30 per visit, which at daily frequency is $325 to $650 per restroom per month.

items: Entry and reception: highest grit load; walk-off mats and daily dust mopping protect LVT wear layers and reduce scratching that makes floors look dirty even when clean.
Treatment corridors: rolling device carts and stools scuff vinyl; expect a quarterly scrub-and-recoat or machine burnish program at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized.
Laser and procedure rooms: dust on device housings and ceiling vents matters because plume residue and particulate collect on horizontal surfaces; high dusting should be weekly, not monthly.
Retail display: glass shelves and product testers show fingerprints immediately; add interior glass service at $15 to $35 per visit if your vendor does not include it.
Staff breakroom: small but heavily used during back-to-back clinic days; breakroom sanitation adds $12 to $25 per visit.

blocks.text: For any suite performing biopsies, excisions, or injectables, five nightly visits per week is the defensible standard. Exam surfaces are cleaned between patients by clinical staff, but nightly terminal-style cleaning by the janitorial crew covers floors, restrooms, waste, sinks, and the surfaces staff miss. Aesthetic-only medspas that perform facials, lasers, and injectables on four clinic days can often justify four visits per week aligned to clinic days, which most vendors price at roughly the three-times-weekly multiplier with 17.3 visits per month.

items.name: Map clinic days to cleaning nights
items.text: Schedule service for every night following a patient day. Closed days need no visit, but Monday mornings after a Saturday clinic should not be skipped.

items.name: Separate clinical and janitorial duties in writing
items.text: Spell out that staff wipe treatment tables between patients and the vendor handles nightly floors, restrooms, high-touch points, and trash, so nobody assumes the other party covered the procedure room.

items.name: Price restrooms and add-ons separately
items.text: Ask bidders to quote base area, per-restroom charges, consumables, and quarterly floor care as separate lines so you can compare like for like.

items.name: Review after 90 days
items.text: Use inspection scores and staff feedback to decide whether a fifth night or an added day porter shift during clinic hours is worth the cost.

blocks.text: Chemical and dispenser choices change labor time and supply cost. A hospital-grade neutral quaternary disinfectant such as Diversey Virex II 256 dilutes at 1:256 from a one-gallon concentrate and is safe on LVT and most treatment-table vinyl, which keeps chemical cost per visit low; confirm the vendor follows the label dwell time rather than spray-and-wipe. For lobby glass and retail fixtures where a disinfectant is not required, an EPA Safer Choice plant-based cleaner like ECOS Pro Orange Plus keeps VOCs low near patients with sensitive skin. In patient restrooms, a battery-powered touchless dispenser such as the Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-inch unit reduces touch points and fits ADA depth limits, and its roll capacity cuts the number of refill trips.

blocks.title: Ask who supplies consumables
blocks.text: Consumables included in the contract typically add $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit, or about $38 to $80 per night for a 3,200 sq ft suite. Practices with heavy restroom use often save by buying paper and soap directly and having the crew stock it.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to clean a 3,000 sq ft dermatology office per month?
faqs.a: At national average rates with LVT flooring and three restrooms, expect roughly $4,000 to $7,000 per month for three visits a week and $6,400 to $11,000 per month for five nightly visits. The model multiplies per-visit price by 4.33 weeks per month, so five nights equals 21.65 visits. High-cost metros add 15 to 40 percent on top of these figures.

faqs.q: Does a medspa need a medical cleaning company or will a standard janitorial vendor do?
faqs.a: A standard commercial vendor can serve a medspa if it trains staff on OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), offers hepatitis B vaccination to exposed employees, maintains Safety Data Sheets under HazCom, and uses EPA-registered disinfectants at label dwell times. Ask for training records and a certificate of insurance naming your practice as additional insured before signing.

faqs.q: Is sharps and medical waste disposal included in the cleaning price?
faqs.a: No. Janitorial contracts almost always exclude regulated medical waste, sharps containers, and biohazard bags. Those go to a licensed medical waste hauler. Your cleaning scope should state that crews never handle sharps containers and only remove ordinary trash and recycling.

faqs.q: Why did my bid come in higher than the per-sq-ft rate for offices?
faqs.a: Treatment rooms take longer per square foot than open office space, hard floors need damp mopping on every visit, and patient restrooms run at a higher density. Vendors also price in disinfectant dwell time and after-hours access. A derm or medspa bid 20 to 35 percent above a general office of the same size is normal.

faqs.q: Can we cut costs by cleaning four nights instead of five?
faqs.a: If your suite is closed one weekday, yes. Four visits per week is about 17.3 visits per month, which cuts the monthly bill by roughly 20 percent compared with five nights. Do not skip a night after a procedure day, and make sure the contract defines what happens after holiday closures.
